requirements.text: Choose the author "Albert Einstein" and let the postback reload complete before using the tag list (no race with the reload).
Choose the tag "inspirational" from the reloaded tag list, waiting for or checking that it is offered.
Press Search and wait for the results (the second postback) to load before reading them.
Return every quote shown as a list of typed objects with the quote's text, its author and the tag.
When no quote matches, return an empty list (not an error) and say so.

When the page does not behave as described (no reload, tag not offered, results never load, site unreachable), fail with an error that says which step failed and what was seen, never converting such a failure into a normal result.

Tell a genuine no-match apart from a broken or changed results page: an empty result is confirmed by the page's no-result state (or the absence of the results heading), not inferred from a locator matching nothing.
Close everything the program opened (connection/Run/page, or browser/context) on every path, errors included.

programs.notes: Clean step-wrapped flow: waits for the tag option after the author postback, networkidle after Search, typed errors with step and observed, everything closed via await using plus finish(). When no .quote appears within 3 s it returns [] with no check of the page's no-result state, so a changed layout reads as 'no match'.

site_errors: Waits for the Search postback's response at /search.aspx, but Search posts to /filter.aspx, so that expect_response would time out.
programs.notes: It waits for the author postback's response and load, checks the chosen values, and wraps every step in a FormStepError naming the step and the options seen; the with-blocks close everything. An empty .quote list is returned without confirming a genuine no-match.

A thorough flow: it waits for the tag option, then for the filter.aspx response during the click and for the load state, validates each quote's author and tag, and closes page, Run and connection on every path. A count of zero returns Ok(empty) with no check that the page really reports no match.

The author/tag dependency is handled by waiting for the tag option after selecting the author, and closing is correct. After Search, a TimeoutError waiting for the first div.quote is swallowed and returns [], so results that never load (slow site, failed postback, changed layout) are reported as 'no match' instead of an error.

Same shape as its Python sibling: it waits for the tag option, then clicks Search. A TimeoutError waiting for the first visible .quote is caught and turned into an empty result, which masks a slow or broken results page as no match; context and browser are closed in finally.
